statement: A residual proper-homology detector lies in the Prym kernel and cannot occur in a genus-one compactified cover. Punctured elliptic transport requires an entire fibre in the boundary, which forces deg(f) <= deg(Y/U). Under the exact target normalizer theorem a detecting such map excludes the subgroup. Explicit detecting quotients can fail the fibre condition, and adding punctures need not lift arithmetic normalizers.
where_proved: sections/g_cover_transport.tex, G.22; input at end of sections/G.tex
depends_on: The Stacks Project, Section53.12, Lemmas53.12.2 and53.12.4
manuscript_passages: Modern prompt G(b),(d), full profinite cases
Explicit follow-up: finite-cover homology detection and transport through a CM Jacobian quotient
notes: The target criterion is used only for a pointed curve becoming isomorphic to (E,O) over a finite extension, or under an expressly separate theorem for that target. No transfer to an arbitrary isogenous elliptic curve, different CM field, or higher-dimensional CM factor is claimed. Exact polynomial certificate: code/g_cover_transport.py and g_cover_transport.json. This narrows but does not settle G.20.
